fields.spec_version: JEDEC JESD79-3C — DDR3 SDRAM Standard (November 2008; revision of JESD79-3B April 2008)

spec_lineage_ddrx.summary: Original SDRAM, JEDEC JESD21-C; single-data-rate, 3.3 V LVTTL, 64 Mb–256 Mb densities.
DDR1; SSTL_2 2.5 V; 2n prefetch; bidirectional DQS; BL2/BL4/BL8; up to DDR-400.
DDR2; SSTL_18 1.8 V; 4n prefetch; differential DQS introduced; BL4/BL8; up to DDR2-800/1066; on-die termination introduced.
DDR3; SSTL_15 1.5 V; 8n prefetch; fly-by topology; mandatory differential DQS; BC4/BL8; up to DDR3-1600 in base spec; RESET# pin added; ZQ calibration.
DDR4; pseudo-open-drain LVSTL_12 at 1.2 V; 8n prefetch but with bank groups; up to DDR4-3200.
DDR5; 1.1 V VDD; bank-group + sub-channel; up to DDR5-6400 base / DDR5-8400 in 2023 addenda.

previous_versions_of_this_spec.summary: Added MR3 Multi Purpose Register, expanded speed bins, write leveling clarifications, 1 Gb / 2 Gb density definitions.
ASR / SRT extensions, ODT timing refinements, 4 Gb density support, x16 ballout updates; differences from JESD79-3B documented in Annex A.

key_changes_vs_ddr2.impact: BL8 fixed or BC4 on-the-fly; minimum 8-beat transfer at the DRAM array → 4 nCK tCCD.
Common-mode noise rejection at higher data rates.
Better signal integrity at ≥ 800 MT/s; requires Write Leveling per DRAM to compensate flight-time skew.
Eliminates the DDR2 cold-power-up requirement; DRAM can be asynchronously reset at any time.
≈30% lower IDD; SSTL_15 signaling instead of SSTL_18.
Output driver Ron and ODT Rtt tracked to a 240 Ω reference; corrects VT drift in service.
Termination strength changes for write bursts without an extra MRS.

key_changes_vs_ddr2.change: MPR (Multi Purpose Register) added in JESD79-3B
key_changes_vs_ddr2.impact: Read-side training via predefined pattern; replaces the ad-hoc DDR2 training methods.

key_changes_vs_ddr2.change: Burst length fixed BL8 or chopped BC4 only
key_changes_vs_ddr2.impact: DDR2's BL4 fixed is replaced; BC4 still chops the burst but the internal core access is still 8n.

backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR3 SO-DIMM / UDIMM has a different notch position than DDR2 to prevent insertion of the wrong DIMM type.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Plugging DDR3 into a DDR2 socket (or vice versa) can damage the DRAM due to VDD mismatch (1.5 V vs 1.8 V).

backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR3 requires RESET# to be asserted LOW at power-up and during the initialization sequence; DDR2 used a power-stable cold-start without an explicit reset.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A DDR3 controller that omits RESET# control will see undefined DRAM state on power-up; initialization MRS may be silently misregistered.

backward_compat_traps.rule: JESD79-3C specifies MRS sequence MR2 → MR3 → MR1 → MR0 during init (with DLL Reset bit in MR0). Reordering can leave the DLL in an undefined state.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Many DDR3 controllers write MR0 first (carry-over DDR2 habit) — the DLL Reset bit may then be honoured before MR1 enables the DLL.

backward_compat_traps.rule: DDR3 DIMMs use fly-by routing; per-DRAM flight-time skew can exceed 1 tCK at DDR3-1600. Write Leveling is the controller's only way to compensate.
backward_compat_traps.trap: DDR3 controllers that omit Write Leveling work on point-to-point boards but fail (intermittently) on multi-rank DIMMs at high speed grades.

backward_compat_traps.rule: ZQCL must be issued at the end of init and ZQCS periodically. Without ZQ calibration, Ron / Rtt drift and signal integrity degrades.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Skipping ZQCS for tens of minutes at elevated temperature can cause read errors that recover only after the next ZQCS.

backward_compat_traps.rule: After Self-Refresh exit, the controller must issue one extra REF before re-entering Self-Refresh — covers internal timer drift.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Controllers that re-enter SR immediately after a brief wake will miss this constraint; over time, cell content may be lost.

backward_compat_traps.rule: MR1 A0=1 (DLL off) supports only CL=6 and CWL=6. Other CL/CWL settings are illegal in DLL-off mode.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Reusing DLL-on MR0/MR2 settings after disabling DLL produces undefined DRAM behaviour.

backward_compat_traps.rule: CK frequency may be changed only in Self-Refresh OR Precharge Power-Down; outside these states the clock must remain stable within jitter/SSC limits.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Dynamic-frequency-scaling controllers that change CK without entering SR/PPD will see undefined DRAM behaviour.

fields.version_naming_history_note: DDR3 is the third generation of Double Data Rate SDRAM standardized by JEDEC under the JC-42.3 task group on DRAM components. JESD79-3 (June 2007) was the initial release; JESD79-3C (November 2008) is the current major revision encompassing the JEDEC standard at the time of this document. Low-voltage variants DDR3L (1.35 V) and DDR3U (1.25 V) are addenda (JESD79-3-1, JESD79-3-1A). DDR3 was superseded by DDR4 (JESD79-4, 2012) and DDR5 (JESD79-5, 2020) in the JEDEC roadmap, but DDR3 remains in production for embedded / industrial / automotive markets.
